reasons: Graded as no-executable-plan (B). The plan does not present an unestablished outcome as established: price $500 is ASSUMED, close_rate UNKNOWN, validation.decides = CURRENT_DEMAND, OFFER_AND_PRICE, CONVERSION, FULFILMENT. Four discovered openings, each with public citations that checked out (WebFetch): Loganix GBP Audit & Optimization $259, white-label, 'most within seven business days' (verified); Contra GBP full reset from $397, 5 days (verified); Merchynt one-time $300-$500 and $125-$400/month (verified); WPZOOM one-page site $500-$1,500 (verified). The Merchynt, OfficeConsumer and HomeASAP prices that Brain's gate rejected are not used as established (the price stays ASSUMED and HomeASAP is excluded). Each opening gets its own decisive link: the Loganix resale fails on buyer price, demand and conversion, with the fulfiller still to confirm; Merchynt one-time on fulfilment ($60 was an agent-facing price); the retainer on settlement in the window and unknown fulfiller cost; the website on having no buyer-paid price and no costed fulfiller. All of these agree with the context links. Experiment: Loganix written confirmation on day 1, then 80 emails, and prepaid orders counted by day 7. It costs $0, takes 3.0 owner hours in week 1 and 8.0 in total over the window, which is at most 9, and ends on day 7, well inside 21. Proof is Loganix confirming plus at least 3 prepaid orders by day 7; stop is fewer than 2, a Loganix refusal, a payout after day 19, or more than 3 owner hours in a week. Arithmetic: 7 x $500 = $3,500 gross, settled by day 19 (day-5 payment + 14-day upper bound from Stripe docs, verified); 7 x $259 = $1,813 is paid from the settled payout, so $0 is tied up; $1,687 net, or about $1,583 after card fees, which still clears $1,500. Weaknesses that do not fail the rubric: (1) exactly 2 prepaid orders by day 7 matches neither proof nor stop (the gap is ambiguous; the rubric's text, 'states its proof rule and stop rule', is met); (2) Stripe fees are not in the cash ledger; (3) delivery lands about day 28-30, after the window, which risks refunds; (4) Loganix also sells direct to local businesses at $259, which undercuts the $500 resale. OFFER_AND_PRICE is correctly among the decided links.

Graded as no-executable-plan (B). Price, deposit rate and bookkeeper cost are all UNKNOWN; the 22 jobs is an ESTIMATE; validation.decides = CURRENT_DEMAND, OFFER_AND_PRICE, CONVERSION, FULFILMENT, ECONOMICS. Nothing is presented as established. Three discovered openings with public citations, checked by WebFetch: Xendoo catch-up 'Starting at $295/Month' (verified; the plan's note that the unit is ambiguous is fair); Bench catch-up free with annual plans from $1,910/yr, turnaround 2 weeks to 1 month (verified); Freelancer.com website-design category with 348 jobs, redesigns at $283-$656 average bids with 300-400 bids each, and store builds at $390 (421 bids) and $437 (337 bids) (all verified on the cited page); Instantly Growth $47 with 1,000 contacts and Hypergrowth $107 with 25,000 contacts (verified, though s5's claim text omits Hypergrowth); Stripe first payout 7-14 days (verified). Each opening gets its own decisive link: bookkeeping lacks a buyer-paid price, demand, a deposit rate and a fulfiller cost; the redesign and Shopify openings have an assumed price contradicted by public bid levels. Experiment: $77 at risk ($47 + $30), owner-approved, loss bounded at $77 on STOP. It finishes on day 18, well inside 45, and the further $107 is spent only after proof. Proof is at least 5 paid $600 deposits from 1,000 contacts plus 3 bookkeeper quotes at or under $600 with 14-day turnaround. Stop is fewer than 3 deposits, quotes over $600 or 14 days, or no sale after day 28; 3-4 deposits are handled explicitly with a re-decide on day 21. The decision it triggers is stated. Arithmetic, recomputed: 22 x $1,200 = $26,400 minus $13,200 bookkeepers, $778.80 Stripe and $184 tools leaves $12,237.20, at least $12,000 even on the stricter net reading. Peak owner money is under $1,000 because deposits settle by day 32, before bookkeepers are paid on day 42; this is within $2,500. The last balance settles on day 44, at or before 45. Weaknesses that do not fail the rubric: (1) zero slack at the deadline edge; (2) the continuation needs about 49 owner hours of scoping calls, which is left UNKNOWN rather than gated (the objective sets no hours limit); (3) the day-18 rate is applied to a shorter 3-9-day close window for the second batch; (4) the 9-day warm-up of new domains and cold-email deliverability are unmeasured.
